_README: Generated from measured evidence, then edited by hand. See the P1.1 session document.
Mechanically derived: `databases` is which fixture databases the command ACTUALLY queried at
runtime (observed by patching better-sqlite3's prepare), not which env vars its imports mention.
Static reference proved useless as a proxy: env-var names gave 30 database-dependent commands and
broad signals gave 84, where reading imports had suggested 42. None of those is a dependency.
Judgement calls -- every Tier C classification -- carry their own `note` explaining why a fixture
`python` and `powershell` commands are marked measured-by-outcome: the observer only instruments
better-sqlite3, so for those the evidence is that they PASS in a clean clone with no database
present, which is exactly what Tier F requires of them.

requires._why: the test asserts rows.length > 1, so the series must span more than one year
the baseline row the test looks up by year === 2017; the plan filters this offense
an INNER JOIN in the plan's first CTE -- an agency absent here contributes nothing

THE clause that makes this test non-vacuous. Its final loop is guarded by `if (base[column] !== null)`, and the plan's series CTE filters `population IS NOT NULL` and divides by SUM(population). With no non-null 2017 population every indexed column is NULL, the guard never opens, and the test passes having evaluated no equality at all.

entries.finding: FINDING (open, needs a product decision): this test asserts a NATIONAL query is left unrewritten. That holds only on a machine with NO rollup database. With any rollup database present -- including an empty fixture, and including production -- optimizeNibrsSql rewrites summary_clearance_type to rollup.national_summary_clearance_type and the assertion fails. So the test currently passes because of what is ABSENT from the developer's disk. Whether the optimizer or the expectation is wrong is a product call and is not decided here.

proves the verifier GOVERNS Tier C execution rather than sitting beside it: one positive control that a child process reaches a verified published set, then eleven attempts to reach a corpus without verification (bootstrap-pending, stale, hash-mismatched, absent, unknown, path-escaping, mixed-set, no pointer, identity mismatch, unverified-at-acquisition, empty declaration), each required to yield NO environment. Also certifies the strengthened schema fingerprint. Tier F: builds its own throwaway SQLite databases and its own local registry, needs no corpus, and never contacts production.

session-analytics credential containment. Imports lib/analytics-auth.ts and CALLS the authorization decision for every rejection case -- no header, malformed header, the obsolete tracked literal, an unrelated key, and any credential in a query string including a correct one -- plus fail-closed on absent/empty ANALYTICS_PASSWORD and the single Bearer accept. Also spawns all five stress/eval/smoke/canary tools with --print-target, with every ambient target variable scrubbed for bare controls and set to production for the env-independence controls, to prove a bare invocation resolves to localhost and an explicit production URL is still honoured, without contacting anything. The two unavoidable source-placement assertions read BOTH the index blob and the tracked working tree and name the failing view. Tier F: no database, no corpus, no network.

handler-level wiring and database-boundary evidence for /api/session-analytics. Sets QUERY_LOG_DB_PATH to its own temporary SQLite fixture and ANALYTICS_PASSWORD/QUERY_LOG_KEY before importing the route, patches Database.prototype.prepare and .exec before that import, then invokes the REAL exported GET: no header, absent and empty analytics key, malformed and wrong Bearer values, the obsolete literal, a distinct query-log-shaped key, and every governed URL credential name alongside the correct Bearer key -- all 401 with an identical body and ZERO recorded database operations, which also means no handle was opened. The correct dedicated Bearer key then returns 200 carrying rows that exist only in the fixture, which is the recorder's positive control, and that response emits no allow-origin header while the module exports no OPTIONS handler. Tier F: builds its own throwaway SQLite fixture, needs no corpus, and never contacts production.

P1.4c: the artifact manifest. buildRecord is a PURE function over a stat-like object, so the symlink and executable-bit branches are exercised on any platform; walkRelease is the only filesystem-dependent part. Covers determinism (order-independent, sorted by raw bytes not locale, path-independent), the exclusion policy closed at both document and entry level, that no default exclusion set exists to fall back on, and that a change to an excluded path leaves the digest still while a change to an included path moves it and names the path. Real symlink and executable-bit behaviour runs in a Linux container when one is available and is otherwise reported as a MANDATORY PRE-DEPLOYMENT PROBE rather than claimed. Tier F: no database, no corpus, no network, temp directories only.

P1.4c: the receipt. Builds a throwaway git repository, exports the commit blob by blob, adds what a build produces, then drives the SHIPPED generator and verifier. Covers the closed receipt schema, the closed NEXT_PUBLIC_ build-input set (and that no other env name or value reaches the receipt or even an error message), node_modules and the native module being digested, artifact change with source unchanged, a receipt being unable to widen its own exclusions in either direction, a forged policy digest, missing git objects and an absent policy both yielding unverified, and the BOOTSTRAP composition: the generator and verifier executing from the exported release rather than the operations checkout. Tier F: temp directories only.

P1.4c: the verifier. /proc readers are injected so per-pid reporting -- where a partial reload is either surfaced or lost -- is exercised without /proc. Covers the verdict lattice (fail dominates unverified), L1 never inferred, the two distinct refusal sentences, L4 symlink resolution, a split reload reported per pid with healthy workers unblamed, worker-count disagreement, executable-digest and DELETED-image reporting including the PM2-daemon hazard where versions agree but binaries differ, that half A never compares a digest across platforms, that a receiptless legacy release is unverified and never blocks a rollback, and that only L2 and L3 gate publication with no automatic rollback anywhere. Tier F: temp directories only.

P1.4a: the release input must be an exact commit exported from Git objects. Builds throwaway repositories in a temp directory and drives the SHIPPED scripts/lib/release-export.sh, the same file the deploy sources -- the prune-releases.sh precedent, so the test cannot pass against a drifted copy. Covers full-SHA-only input, ancestry against origin/<branch>, per-path blob equality against the commit tree with export-ignore and export-subst as the decisive mutations, a whole-file Git LFS pointer refusal proven to fire while blob equality still passes on the same blob, near-miss and quoted-format controls so the refusal is structural rather than a grep, and the closed post-export allowlist with its schema mutations. Dual-view (index blob and worktree) source assertions confirm the deploy sources the library and that rsync, chmod and cp -al are gone. Tier F: no database, no corpus, no network, no state outside its own temp directories; needs a POSIX bash, located explicitly from git.exe on Windows.

P1.3-R: closes the accounting gap reconcile() structurally cannot see. Walks scripts/ recursively for test-shaped basenames (a segment exactly `test`, split on - and _, extensions ts/js/py/ps1, .d.ts excluded), then requires discovered == registered (+) excluded as a DISJOINT UNION with all three sets derived at run time -- filesystem, derived plan, exclusion registry -- and no expected total asserted anywhere. Also validates the exclusion registry against closed kind and reason_code sets, refuses a corpus declaration on an excluded file, requires a non-empty follow_up on any quarantine, refuses a file present in both homes, and requires each registered discovered file to be reachable exactly once. Carries the false-refusal controls too: directory names, `latest`/`contest`/`testing` substrings, .d.ts files and non-governed extensions must all stay out. Tier F: reads package.json, the manifest, the registry and the filesystem; no database, no corpus, no network.

P1.2b dependency closure. Proves the harness Python environment is declared in the repository and cannot drift. Measures the third-party closure from source -- following local-module imports TRANSITIVELY, reading FUNCTION-LEVEL imports through a full AST walk, and including scripts that plan commands SPAWN, discovered dynamically from command source rather than from any hard-coded list, because the four tools carrying `import requests` are network-optional exclusions that nothing reasoning about the plan can see. Requires FORWARD containment (everything imported is declared or reasonably excluded) and REVERSE containment (every locked distribution is reachable from the declaration through the lock's own `# via` provenance, so an extra pinned-and-hashed package fails). The anthropic exclusion is CALL-PATH specific and re-checked every run: it holds only while every harness-reachable invocation of the two tools importing it passes --print-target. Also asserts the lock is fully pinned and hashed and records its generating interpreter and pip-tools version, and that the workflow builds an isolated venv, proves the direct packages absent before installing, installs exclusively from the lock with --require-hashes, runs pip check, compares the installed set to the lock, and names no package or version itself. Tier F: reads source, the declaration, the lock and the workflow; installs nothing, contacts no index, and imports no third-party package.
